newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS STEADY-OFF $1.50 - DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS STEADY-OFF $1.50 - DEALERS.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were steady to mostly $1.00 to $1.50 per cwt lower amid light packer demand which offset potential support from slower marketings, livestock dealers said.
Several packer buyers reportedly had enough hogs lined up through Friday and were starting to bid $0.50 to $1.00 lower for Monday, the dealers said.
"I'm getting a few hogs coming in today, but it is pretty slow," an interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog buyer said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $1.00 lower at $54.00-$55.50 in the country and $56.50-$57.00 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady in light volume at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 to $57.50 at plants.
"It's pretty quiet, with not much happening," one Illinois livestock dealer said.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 to $1.50 lower at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at those plants that were still buying hogs.
Ohio hogs sold $1.00 lower at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, but not many hogs were moving, sources there said.
